intent.raw_query: Japan family with kids, $4500, cherry blossom season 2026, 10 days from NYC

selected_hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the iconic Japanese tradition of hanami (flower viewing) beneath hundreds of cherry blossom trees in Kyoto's most famous park. The centerpiece weeping cherry tree is illuminated at night, creating a magical atmosphere. Bring a picnic blanket, enjoy local street food stalls, and immerse yourself in this beloved cultural tradition with locals and families.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most significant Buddhist temple, dating back to 628 AD. Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon Thunder Gate, explore the vibrant Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional crafts and snacks, and participate in omikuji fortune-telling. A perfect blend of history, spirituality, and family fun that captures the essence of old Tokyo.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: A profoundly moving and historically essential experience for families. Tour the Peace Memorial Museum to understand the events of August 6, 1945, walk through the Peace Memorial Park, and see the preserved Atomic Bomb Dome. The museum offers child-friendly exhibits and the park provides space for reflection. Combine with a short ferry ride to the stunning Miyajima Island and its famous floating torii gate.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Embark on a self-guided or guided culinary adventure through the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, one of the world's greatest food destinations. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, matcha ice cream, and seasonal Japanese street foods. Kids and adults alike will love the vibrant atmosphere, and it's an authentic deep-dive into Japanese food culture and daily life.

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Stroll through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most iconic and photogenic landscapes, especially beautiful during cherry blossom season. Extend the adventure with a visit to the Iwatayama Monkey Park, where families can interact with Japanese macaques while enjoying panoramic views of Kyoto. Finish with a boat ride along the Oi River for a complete and memorable family day.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and travel time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Kansai International Airport at 13:00. Take the Haruka Express train to Kyoto Station (approx. 75 min, ~¥1,900). Check in to your boutique stay near Maruyama Park in the Gion district. Drop off luggage and take a gentle stroll through Maruyama Park to see late cherry blossoms — the park is famous for its iconic weeping cherry tree and is free to enter.
day_by_day.evening: Walk through the atmospheric stone-paved lanes of Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka (Ninen-zaka & Sannen-zaka), lined with traditional shops and lanterns. Explore the beginning of the Gion district along Hanamikoji Street to soak in the geisha district ambiance.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a bento box at the airport convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart, ~¥500–¥800)
meals.lunch: Pick up an affordable bento or onigiri at Kyoto Station's convenience store or food basement (Isetan B1F) before heading to the hotel (~¥500–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Ramen at Kyoto Ramen Koji (Kyoto Station 10F) or a local ramen shop near Gion — try Kyoto-style chicken broth ramen (~¥900–¥1,200)

day_by_day.notes: Buy an IC card (Suica or ICOCA) at the airport for easy transit payments. Keep receipts for budget tracking. April 15 may still have late cherry blossoms — Maruyama Park is one of the best spots in Kyoto.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine early morning (free entry). Hike through the iconic thousands of vermillion torii gates up the mountain trail. The full hike takes 2–3 hours, but even a 45-minute walk to the first summit offers stunning views. Go early to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to central Kyoto and visit Tofuku-ji Temple (¥500 entry) with its beautiful Zen gardens and moss-covered grounds. Walk north to Sanjusangendo Hall (¥600 entry) to see 1,001 life-size golden warrior statues — one of Japan's most awe-inspiring cultural sights.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion for an evening walk. Watch for maiko (apprentice geisha) near Hanamikoji Street around dusk (5–7 PM). Browse the covered Nishiki Market area if you walk toward central Kyoto.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near the hotel — onigiri, tamagoyaki, and green tea (~¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Inari sushi (inarizushi) near Fushimi Inari — a local specialty sold at stalls near the shrine entrance (~¥300–¥600)
meals.dinner: Tofu cuisine (yudofu) at an affordable restaurant in the Higashiyama area — Kyoto is famous for its tofu dishes (~¥800–¥1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for Fushimi Inari hike. Bring water. The hike can be muddy after rain. Fushimi Inari is free and open 24 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Higashiyama historic district on foot — start at Kiyomizudera Temple (¥500 entry), a UNESCO World Heritage Site with a famous wooden stage jutting out over a hillside. The surrounding cherry blossom trees may still be blooming. Arrive early (by 8 AM) to beat weekend crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill through Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka lanes, browsing local craft shops. Visit Kodai-ji Temple (¥600 entry) with its beautiful bamboo grove and garden. Continue to Chion-in Temple (free entry to outer grounds) — one of Japan's largest temple gates (Sanmon).
day_by_day.evening: Picnic in Maruyama Park (right next to your hotel!) — buy food from nearby stalls or a convenience store. The park is especially magical at night with lantern-lit cherry blossom trees. Free entry.

meals.breakfast: Morning set at a local kissaten (Japanese coffee shop) near Gion — coffee and toast with egg (~¥500–¥700)
meals.lunch: Street food along Ninenzaka — matcha soft cream, yatsuhashi (cinnamon wafer), or grilled skewers (~¥500–¥800)
meals.dinner: Convenience store picnic in Maruyama Park — onigiri, karaage chicken, edamame, and a can of beer or tea (~¥600–¥1,000)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday will be busy at Kiyomizudera — arrive before 8:30 AM. The Higashiyama area is very walkable and most sights are within 1–2 km of each other and your hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nara (45 min from Kyoto by Kintetsu Express, ~¥680 one way). Visit Nara Park (free) and meet the famous free-roaming sacred deer. Feed them shika senbei (deer crackers, ¥200). Walk to Todai-ji Temple (¥600) to see the giant bronze Buddha — one of Japan's national treasures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kasuga Taisha Shrine (free outer grounds, ¥500 for inner sanctum) — a UNESCO site famous for its hundreds of bronze and stone lanterns. Walk through the peaceful Kasugayama Primeval Forest trail (free). Visit Kofuku-ji Temple and its five-story pagoda (free exterior).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by early evening. Relax and explore the local Gion area. Visit a neighborhood sento (public bath) for an authentic Japanese bathing experience (~¥500–¥800).

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel area bakery before departing for Nara (~¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf sushi) — Nara's local specialty available at shops near Kintetsu Nara Station (~¥800–¥1,200)
meals.dinner: Gyudon (beef rice bowl) at Yoshinoya or Sukiya near Kyoto Station or Gion (~¥500–¥700)

day_by_day.notes: Buy the Kintetsu Nara round-trip ticket at Kyoto Station. The deer in Nara Park are wild — be careful with food and bags. Nara is very family-friendly and children love the deer.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Arashiyama district in western Kyoto (30 min by bus from Gion, ~¥230). Walk through the famous Arashiyama Bamboo Grove (free) in the morning light. Visit Tenryu-ji Temple and Garden (¥500) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site with a stunning pond garden framed by cherry blossoms and mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the scenic Togetsukyo Bridge and walk along the Oi River. Explore the hillside Jojakko-ji Temple (¥500) with its moss-covered steps and pagoda. Visit Okochi Sanso Villa Garden (¥1,000) for panoramic views of Kyoto — includes free matcha tea and sweets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion and explore Pontocho Alley — a narrow lantern-lit lane parallel to the Kamo River, lined with affordable restaurants and izakayas. Great for a budget dinner with atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a convenience store before heading to Arashiyama (~¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Yudofu (tofu hot pot) at a restaurant near Tenryu-ji — Arashiyama has several affordable lunch sets (~¥800–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Yakitori (grilled chicken skewers) and draft beer at an izakaya in Pontocho Alley (~¥1,000–¥1,800 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Take Bus 11 or 28 from Gion to Arashiyama. The Bamboo Grove is most beautiful and least crowded before 8 AM. Pontocho is best explored on foot — it's a narrow alley only for pedestrians.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku no Michi) — a scenic 2 km canal-side walk lined with hundreds of cherry trees (late bloomers may still be visible). Walk from Ginkaku-ji (Silver Pavilion, ¥500) southward, passing small shrines, cafes, and local gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Nanzen-ji Temple complex (free outer grounds, ¥600 for Hojo garden) — one of Kyoto's most important Zen temples. Explore the massive Sanmon gate (¥600 to climb) for rooftop views. Walk through the surprisingly photogenic red-brick Suirokaku Aqueduct (free, part of the temple grounds).
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Nishiki Market (Kyoto's Kitchen) — a 400-meter covered market with over 100 stalls selling pickles, tofu, street food, and local snacks. Great for budget grazing and souvenir shopping. Open until around 6 PM for most stalls.

meals.breakfast: Bakery near the Philosopher's Path — several charming local bakeries open early (~¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Soba noodles at a restaurant near Nanzen-ji — cold zaru soba is a Kyoto specialty (~¥700–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Karaage (Japanese fried chicken) and rice set at a local teishoku restaurant near Gion (~¥700–¥1,200)

day_by_day.notes: The Philosopher's Path is about 3 km northeast of your hotel — walkable or take a bus. Nishiki Market is near Shijo-Kawaramachi and easily reached by bus. Great for picking up affordable snacks and local food souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Osaka (15 min by Shinkansen or 30 min by Hankyu Express from Kyoto, ~¥560 one way on Hankyu). Visit Osaka Castle (¥600 for main tower museum) — a stunning feudal castle surrounded by a moat and parkland with possible late cherry blossoms. Explore the castle museum inside for Edo-period history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Dotonbori entertainment district — Osaka's most iconic area with neon signs, the Glico Running Man, and street food. Cross the Dotonbori canal bridge and explore the arcade streets. Visit Shinsaibashi shopping arcade for window shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Eat your way through Dotonbori street food before returning to Kyoto. Osaka is famous for being Japan's food capital — try multiple cheap street foods for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near your Kyoto hotel before departing (~¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Takoyaki (octopus balls) and kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers) from Dotonbori street stalls — Osaka's iconic foods (~¥600–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Okonomiyaki (savory pancake) at a budget restaurant in Dotonbori — Osaka-style with toppings (~¥800–¥1,300)

day_by_day.notes: Use the Hankyu Railway from Kyoto-Kawaramachi Station to Osaka Umeda for the most budget-friendly option. Osaka Castle is a short subway ride from Umeda. Return to Kyoto by 9 PM to avoid late trains.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion, ¥500) — Kyoto's most iconic landmark, a gold-leaf-covered Zen temple reflected in a mirror pond. Arrive early (opens at 9 AM) to beat tour groups. Nearby, visit Ryoan-ji Temple (¥600) with its world-famous Zen rock garden — a meditative and culturally significant site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nishiki Tenmangu Shrine (free) and the surrounding Nishiki Market area. Visit Nijo Castle (¥1,030 including garden) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the historic palace of the Tokugawa shoguns with famous 'nightingale floors' that squeak to detect intruders.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening in the Gion district. Visit Yasaka Shrine (free, open 24 hours) — beautifully lit at night and just steps from your hotel in Maruyama Park. Watch for evening cultural activity near the shrine.

meals.breakfast: Obanzai breakfast (Kyoto-style small dishes) at a local diner or hotel area restaurant (~¥600–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Lunch set (teishoku) near Kinkaku-ji or Ryoan-ji area — rice, miso soup, and side dishes (~¥700–¥1,200)
meals.dinner: Sushi at a conveyor belt sushi restaurant (kaiten-zushi) near Shijo — plates from ¥100–¥200 each, budget ~¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Kinkaku-ji and Ryoan-ji are in northwestern Kyoto — take Bus 101 or 205 from central Kyoto (~¥230). Nijo Castle is centrally located and easily reached by subway (Nijo Station on Tozai Line).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Daitoku-ji Temple complex (free outer grounds, individual sub-temples ¥400–¥500) — a large Zen temple complex with multiple sub-temples, beautiful rock gardens, and moss gardens. Less touristy than other major sites — a hidden gem for culture lovers. Explore Zuiho-in and Koto-in sub-temples.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Kitano Tenmangu Shrine (free) — dedicated to the god of learning, with a beautiful plum and cherry tree garden. Walk through the surrounding Nishijin textile district — Kyoto's traditional weaving neighborhood. Visit the Nishijin Textile Center (free) for live kimono weaving demonstrations.
day_by_day.evening: Final Gion evening — splurge slightly on a nicer dinner as a treat. Walk the full length of Hanamikoji Street one more time and visit Gion Hatanaka area for the most atmospheric views of traditional Kyoto machiya townhouses.

meals.breakfast: Japanese-style breakfast at a local kissaten — tamago toast, miso soup, salad set (~¥500–¥800)
meals.lunch: Ramen or udon at a local noodle shop in the Kitano/Nishijin area (~¥700–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Shabu-shabu or sukiyaki at a budget-friendly hot pot restaurant near Gion — look for lunch-price dinner sets (~¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Daitoku-ji is in northern Kyoto — take Bus 101 or 205. The Nishijin Textile Center kimono shows run at set times — check the schedule online. This is a great day for slower-paced cultural immersion.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — revisit your favorite spot near Maruyama Park or take one last walk through the Higashiyama district. Visit any remaining shrines or temples you missed. Buy last-minute souvenirs at Ninenzaka shops or Nishiki Market (open from 9 AM). Budget souvenir ideas: yatsuhashi sweets, matcha kit-kats, local pickles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel (typically by 11 AM — store luggage at the hotel or at Kyoto Station coin lockers, ¥400–¥700). Head to Kyoto Station and take the Haruka Express back to Kansai Airport (allow 2+ hours before your flight). Browse the Kyoto Station Isetan food basement for last-minute food souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Kansai Airport. Enjoy one final Japanese meal at the airport — ramen, sushi, or tonkatsu at the airport restaurants (~¥1,000–¥1,500).

meals.breakfast: Final convenience store breakfast or a sit-down morning set near the hotel (~¥400–¥800)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at Kyoto Station — the station has dozens of affordable options including ekiben (station bento boxes, ¥800–¥1,200) — a great Japanese travel tradition
meals.dinner: Airport dinner before departure — try tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) or soba at Kansai Airport restaurants (~¥1,000–¥1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for the Haruka Express journey and airport check-in/security. Kyoto Station coin lockers fill up quickly on weekends — arrive early. Don't forget to use remaining yen on food, snacks, or last-minute gifts.

trip_options.title: Classic Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use this time to rest on the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Kansai International Airport at 13:00. Take the Haruka Express train to Kyoto Station (~75 min, ~¥3,600). Check in to your Boutique Stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district. Freshen up and take a gentle orientation stroll through the Gion district — explore the iconic Hanamikoji Street lined with traditional machiya townhouses and spot maiko (apprentice geisha) preparing for evening engagements.
day_by_day.evening: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park — just steps from your hotel. Experience your first hanami (flower viewing) beneath Maruyama Park's famous weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura), beautifully illuminated at night. Join locals picnicking under the blossoms for an authentic first evening in Japan.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight
meals.lunch: Grab a bento box or onigiri at a convenience store (7-Eleven or Lawson) at Kyoto Station upon arrival — quick, affordable, and authentically Japanese (¥500–¥900)
meals.dinner: Omen Noodles on Shirakawa-dori near Gion — a beloved local restaurant serving hearty udon noodle sets in a cozy traditional setting (¥1,200–¥1,800 per person)

day_by_day.notes: April 15 is typically within peak cherry blossom season in Kyoto. Maruyama Park is free to enter and open 24 hours. Keep your JR Pass or IC card topped up. Jet lag tip: stay awake until at least 21:00 local time to adjust faster.

day_by_day.morning: Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine — Take a 20-minute train ride (Keihan Line) to Fushimi Inari. Hike the iconic thousands of vermillion torii gates up the sacred mountain. Go early (by 08:00) to beat the crowds. The full hike takes ~2–3 hours but even a 45-minute walk to the first summit offers stunning views and photo opportunities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to central Kyoto and visit Nijo Castle (Nijojo) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site with stunning Edo-period architecture, nightingale floors, and beautifully manicured gardens. Excellent for history lovers and families (admission ~¥1,300 per adult). Nearby Nijo-jo area has lovely cherry blossom-lined moats.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion for a cultural evening. Watch a Maiko performance at Gion Corner (a 50-minute cultural show featuring tea ceremony, ikebana, and traditional dance — book ahead, ~¥3,150 per person). Afterward, stroll Shimbashi-dori, Kyoto's most photogenic lantern-lit canal street.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or nearby Inoda Coffee — a Kyoto institution since 1940 serving Japanese-style breakfast sets with coffee (¥900–¥1,400)
meals.lunch: Tofu kaiseki lunch near Fushimi Inari or a teishoku (set meal) at a local restaurant near Nijo Castle (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Izakaya dinner at Gion Finlandia Bar area or Nishiki Koji — try yakitori skewers, edamame, and cold Sapporo beer at a mid-range izakaya (¥2,000–¥3,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is free to enter and open 24/7. Nijo Castle is closed on Tuesdays. Wear comfortable walking shoes — today involves significant walking. Gion Corner performances typically run at 18:00 and 19:00.

day_by_day.morning: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park — Take the Sagano Line to Arashiyama (~25 min from Kyoto Station). Walk through the mystical bamboo forest at dawn for the most magical, crowd-free experience. Then climb to Iwatayama Monkey Park (admission ~¥550 per adult, ¥250 children) to see wild Japanese macaques and enjoy panoramic views over Arashiyama and the Oi River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Tenryu-ji Temple and its stunning Zen garden (UNESCO World Heritage, admission ~¥500), then rent a rowboat on the Oi River (~¥1,500/30 min) for a relaxing family activity with cherry blossom views along the riverbanks. Browse the charming Togetsukyo Bridge area and souvenir shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto city center. Visit Nishiki Market — Kyoto's 'Kitchen' — a narrow 400-meter covered market with over 100 stalls selling pickles, fresh tofu, grilled skewers, and local snacks. Perfect for grazing and food exploration as a family.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departing — or grab fresh tamagoyaki (rolled omelette) and mochi from Nishiki Market if you visit in the evening instead
meals.lunch: Arashiyama riverside lunch at Yoshida-ya or similar — try yudofu (hot tofu) or soba noodles with mountain vegetable tempura in a scenic garden restaurant (¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Nishiki Market food stroll for dinner — graze on kushikatsu skewers, fresh oysters, dashi-rolled omelette, and wagashi sweets (budget ~¥1,500–¥2,500 per person total)

day_by_day.notes: Arashiyama is very crowded on weekends — arrive before 08:00 for the bamboo grove. The Monkey Park involves a steep 20-minute uphill hike; great for kids but take water. Tenryu-ji garden is one of Japan's finest Zen landscapes.

day_by_day.morning: Philosopher's Path and Higashiyama Cultural Walk — Start at Nanzen-ji Temple (free grounds, ~¥600 for inner sanctum), one of Japan's most important Zen temples with a dramatic aqueduct. Walk the Philosopher's Path — a 2km canal-side trail lined with hundreds of cherry trees in full bloom. A deeply peaceful and iconic Kyoto experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Higashiyama walking route south through Eikan-do, Chion-in (massive temple gate), and Kodai-ji Temple (known for stunning illuminated gardens). End at Kiyomizudera Temple (admission ~¥500) — the wooden stage temple with breathtaking views over Kyoto's skyline framed by cherry blossoms.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the preserved Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka stone-paved lanes below Kiyomizudera — lined with traditional shops selling Kyoto crafts, matcha sweets, and ceramics. Return to Gion for a relaxing evening near your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Cafe Bibliotic Hello! near the Philosopher's Path — a charming local cafe with excellent coffee and pastries (¥800–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Obanzai lunch (Kyoto-style home cooking) at a local restaurant along Higashiyama — seasonal vegetables, tofu, and pickles in a traditional set (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Gion Kappa — a beloved local restaurant near Gion Shijo serving Kyoto cuisine including yudofu, grilled fish, and seasonal vegetables (¥2,500–¥3,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a full walking day covering 6–8km — wear very comfortable shoes. Kiyomizudera can be extremely crowded on weekends; consider visiting in late afternoon when tour groups thin out. The Sannenzaka area is excellent for picking up authentic Kyoto souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nara — Take the JR Nara Line from Kyoto Station (~50 min, ~¥720 one way). Visit Nara Park, home to over 1,200 free-roaming sacred deer (shika) — a magical and fun experience for families. Feed the deer shika senbei crackers (¥200/pack). Walk to Todai-ji Temple, housing the world's largest bronze Buddha statue (admission ~¥600).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kasuga Taisha Grand Shrine — one of Japan's most important Shinto shrines, with thousands of stone and bronze lanterns lining moss-covered forest paths (free outer grounds, ~¥500 inner sanctum). Stroll through Naramachi, the preserved merchant district with traditional machiya townhouses converted into cafes and craft shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by early evening. Enjoy a relaxing evening in Gion — perhaps visit a traditional sento (public bathhouse) for a genuine local experience (~¥500–¥800). Alternatively, enjoy a quiet stroll along the Shirakawa Canal with its weeping cherry trees reflected in the water.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store before departing for Nara
meals.lunch: Kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf sushi) — Nara's signature dish — at Hiraso restaurant near Nara Park, a local institution (¥1,500–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Ramen dinner back in Kyoto — Kyoto-style white miso ramen at Menya Inoichi or similar near Gion (¥900–¥1,400 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Nara deer are wild animals — supervise young children closely and don't tease them with food. Todai-ji is one of Japan's most awe-inspiring buildings. April is an ideal time to visit Nara as cherry blossoms also bloom in Nara Park. Keep your IC card charged for trains.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Kyoto to Hiroshima via Shinkansen — Take the Nozomi/Hikari Shinkansen from Kyoto Station to Hiroshima (~1 hour, covered by JR Pass). Check in to a mid-range hotel near Hiroshima Station or Peace Park area. Head straight to the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park — a profoundly moving and historically essential experience. The museum chronicles the 1945 atomic bombing with deeply personal artifacts and testimonies (admission ~¥200 per adult).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Peace Memorial Park — visit the Atomic Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome), the Children's Peace Monument, and the Memorial Cenotaph. Take a ferry from Hiroshima Port (or Ujina) to Miyajima Island (~10 min, ~¥180 — JR Pass eligible from Hiroshima Pier).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Miyajima Island at golden hour — see the iconic Itsukushima Shrine's floating torii gate (O-torii), one of Japan's most photographed landmarks, beautifully lit at dusk. Stroll the island's charming shopping street and meet the friendly free-roaming deer.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Kyoto before departing or bento from Kyoto Station's Isetan department store basement (¥800–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (layered savory pancake with noodles) at Okonomimura — a multi-floor building dedicated entirely to this Hiroshima specialty (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Grilled oysters and anago (conger eel) on Miyajima Island — both are the island's signature foods, available at restaurants along the main shopping street (¥2,000–¥3,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum is deeply emotional — prepare children aged 8+ with age-appropriate context beforehand. The museum is closed on certain Mondays. The floating torii is most dramatic at high tide — check tide tables in advance. Miyajima is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Miyajima Island early morning if you stayed in Hiroshima — catch the torii gate at low tide when you can walk right up to it (dramatically different from high tide). Hike or take the ropeway up Mt. Misen (~¥1,000 one way) for panoramic views over the Seto Inland Sea and hundreds of islands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Hiroshima and travel to Tokyo via Shinkansen (Nozomi, ~2 hours, covered by JR Pass). Arrive at Tokyo Station and check in to a mid-range hotel in the Asakusa or Shinjuku area. Take the afternoon to settle in and explore your immediate neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: First evening in Tokyo — explore Asakusa neighborhood. Visit Senso-ji Temple at dusk when the lanterns glow and crowds thin. Walk through Nakamise Shopping Street for traditional Japanese souvenirs, snacks, and crafts. Cross Azuma Bridge for views of Tokyo Skytree reflected in the Sumida River.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on Miyajima Island — try freshly grilled oysters or momiji manju (maple leaf-shaped cakes filled with red bean paste) from a street stall (¥500–¥800)
meals.lunch: Ekiben (station bento box) on the Shinkansen from Hiroshima to Tokyo — a beloved Japanese travel tradition with regional specialties (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Asakusa dinner at Sometaro — a charming old-school okonomiyaki restaurant where you cook at your own table (¥1,500–¥2,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Shinkansen seats in advance for the Hiroshima–Tokyo route, especially with families. The journey passes Mt. Fuji on the right side (seats A/B) around Shin-Fuji Station — look out around 14:30–15:00 if departing early afternoon. Asakusa is Tokyo's most traditional district.

day_by_day.morning: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street — Start early (before 08:00) for the most atmospheric experience at Tokyo's oldest temple (founded 628 AD). Walk through the Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate) and the full Nakamise arcade. Explore the temple grounds, Asakusa Shrine, and the traditional craft workshops of Demboin Garden (seasonal access).
day_by_day.afternoon: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — Take the subway to Tsukiji (20 min from Asakusa). Embark on a self-guided culinary adventure through the bustling outer market stalls. Sample fresh tamago (egg) sushi, tamagoyaki, fresh seafood on skewers, Japanese pickles, and matcha desserts. A fantastic hands-on food experience for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Odaiba waterfront — Take the Yurikamome monorail from Shimbashi for a futuristic contrast to the day's traditional experiences. Visit teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets (book ahead, ~¥3,200 per adult) — immersive digital art installations that children and adults find utterly magical. Stunning views of Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo Bay at night.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or fresh taiyaki (fish-shaped cakes) and matcha tea from a stall near Senso-ji (¥300–¥600)
meals.lunch: Self-guided Tsukiji Outer Market grazing lunch — budget ~¥1,500–¥2,500 per person across multiple stalls for sushi, grilled seafood, and Japanese snacks
meals.dinner: Odaiba dinner at Decks Tokyo Beach or Aqua City mall — wide range of mid-range Japanese restaurants with Tokyo Bay views (¥2,000–¥3,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is open daily but most stalls close by early afternoon — arrive by 10:00 for the best selection. teamLab venues require advance booking and often sell out weeks ahead — book before your trip. The Yurikamome monorail offers spectacular views of the Tokyo skyline.

day_by_day.morning: Ueno Park — Tokyo's most famous cherry blossom spot (if blossoms are still present in mid-to-late April). The park houses several world-class museums — visit the Tokyo National Museum (Asia's largest art museum, admission ~¥1,000) for an immersive journey through Japanese history, samurai armor, ancient ceramics, and ukiyo-e woodblock prints. Perfect for history enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Harajuku and Meiji Jingu Shrine — Take the train to Harajuku. Begin with the serene Meiji Jingu Shrine, set in a 70-hectare forested park — a beautiful contrast to the city. Then explore Takeshita Street for quirky Japanese youth fashion, crepes, and pop culture. Walk along Omotesando — Tokyo's elegant tree-lined boulevard — for window shopping and architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Shibuya Crossing and Shinjuku — Experience the world-famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing at rush hour from above (Shibuya Sky observation deck, ~¥2,000, or free from Starbucks). Walk to Shinjuku for dinner in the vibrant Golden Gai alleyways (tiny atmospheric bars) or Kabukicho entertainment district.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a traditional Japanese breakfast set at a nearby kissaten (old-school coffee shop) — eggs, toast, and coffee (¥600–¥900)
meals.lunch: Ueno Ameyoko Market — a lively street market near Ueno Station with food stalls selling fresh sushi, yakitori, and international snacks (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Shinjuku Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — a narrow alley packed with tiny yakitori stalls grilling skewers over charcoal, smoky and atmospheric (¥2,000–¥3,000 per person including drinks)

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free to enter. The forested path to the shrine is one of Tokyo's most peaceful walks. Shibuya Sky requires advance booking on busy days. Golden Gai bars are tiny (some seat only 6 people) and may not be suitable for young children — opt for a family-friendly izakaya instead.

day_by_day.morning: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden — One of Tokyo's finest parks and a top cherry blossom destination (late-blooming varieties may still be in bloom in late April). The garden blends Japanese, French, and English landscape styles across 58 hectares (admission ~¥500). A perfect, peaceful final morning in Japan — ideal for family photos and reflection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute shopping and exploration — Visit Akihabara for electronics, anime, and unique Japanese tech souvenirs. Or head to Ginza for higher-end shopping and the free Tokyo International Forum building (stunning architectural space). Visit Don Quijote (Donki) for affordable Japanese snacks, cosmetics, and quirky souvenirs to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Tokyo. Depart for the airport (Narita: Narita Express ~¥3,070, 60 min / Haneda: Keikyu Line ~¥600, 30 min) — allow at least 3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Reflect on an incredible 10 days of cherry blossoms, history, culture, and family memories across Japan.

meals.breakfast: Final Japanese breakfast — try a traditional set at a hotel or nearby restaurant featuring grilled salmon, miso soup, rice, pickles, and tamagoyaki (¥800–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Ramen farewell lunch at Ichiran or Fuunji in Shinjuku — personal booth ramen, a uniquely Japanese dining experience (¥900–¥1,400)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range Japanese restaurant near your hotel or in Ginza — try a full kaiseki-lite set or tempura course as a final celebratory meal (¥3,000–¥5,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen is closed on Mondays. Alcohol is not permitted in the garden. Pack your largest suitcase the night before to avoid morning stress. Japan Post offices and convenience stores offer luggage forwarding (takuhaibin) to the airport — very convenient for families. Keep ¥2,000–¥3,000 in cash for any remaining transport or small purchases.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the iconic Japanese tradition of hanami (flower viewing) beneath hundreds of cherry blossom trees in Kyoto's most famous park. The centerpiece weeping cherry tree is illuminated at night, creating a magical atmosphere. Bring a picnic blanket, enjoy local street food stalls, and immerse yourself in this beloved cultural tradition with locals and families.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most significant Buddhist temple, dating back to 628 AD. Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon Thunder Gate, explore the vibrant Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional crafts and snacks, and participate in omikuji fortune-telling. A perfect blend of history, spirituality, and family fun that captures the essence of old Tokyo.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: A profoundly moving and historically essential experience for families. Tour the Peace Memorial Museum to understand the events of August 6, 1945, walk through the Peace Memorial Park, and see the preserved Atomic Bomb Dome. The museum offers child-friendly exhibits and the park provides space for reflection. Combine with a short ferry ride to the stunning Miyajima Island and its famous floating torii gate.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Embark on a self-guided or guided culinary adventure through the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, one of the world's greatest food destinations. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, matcha ice cream, and seasonal Japanese street foods. Kids and adults alike will love the vibrant atmosphere, and it's an authentic deep-dive into Japanese food culture and daily life.

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Stroll through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most iconic and photogenic landscapes, especially beautiful during cherry blossom season. Extend the adventure with a visit to the Iwatayama Monkey Park, where families can interact with Japanese macaques while enjoying panoramic views of Kyoto. Finish with a boat ride along the Oi River for a complete and memorable family day.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from the airport to your boutique stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely first stroll through the iconic Maruyama Park to witness the legendary weeping cherry blossom tree (shidarezakura) in full bloom. Absorb the atmosphere of hanami culture as locals and visitors gather beneath the blossoms.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle evening walk through the lantern-lit stone-paved lanes of Gion, Kyoto's most celebrated geisha district. Admire the preserved machiya townhouses and keep an eye out for geiko and maiko on their way to evening engagements. End the evening with a quiet, atmospheric dinner close to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Not applicable (in transit)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Kichisen (Yoshida Sanso area) or Mizai — a Michelin-starred kaiseki restaurant in Kyoto serving exquisite multi-course traditional Japanese cuisine with seasonal spring ingredients and local sake pairings.

day_by_day.notes: April 15 typically falls within peak cherry blossom season in Kyoto. Maruyama Park is especially stunning at night when the weeping cherry tree is illuminated. Book kaiseki dinner well in advance as Michelin-starred restaurants fill quickly during hanami season.

day_by_day.morning: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park — Experience the full hanami tradition with a private guided morning walk through Maruyama Park when crowds are thinnest. Your guide will explain the cultural and historical significance of hanami, pointing out rare cherry tree varieties. Continue to the adjacent Chion-in Temple, one of Japan's most imposing Buddhist structures, for a serene morning visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Higashiyama Historic District on foot — a beautifully preserved hillside neighborhood of traditional shops, tea houses, and shrines. Visit Kiyomizudera Temple perched dramatically on a wooden stage overlooking the city. Browse high-end craft shops along Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka stone-paved lanes for premium ceramics, lacquerware, and textiles.
day_by_day.evening: Private tea ceremony experience at an exclusive Gion tea house, guided by a certified tea master. Dress in optional kimono rental for the full cultural immersion. Followed by a curated omakase dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast featuring Japanese and Western options — fresh seasonal fruit, miso soup, grilled fish, tamagoyaki, and artisan pastries.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Hyotei — a legendary three-Michelin-star restaurant in Nanzenji serving refined kaiseki since 1837, with a special spring cherry blossom menu.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nakamura — one of Kyoto's oldest and most respected kaiseki restaurants (est. 1716), specializing in Kyoto-style kyo-ryori cuisine with bamboo shoots and spring vegetables.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the private tea ceremony and Kiyomizudera entry. Wear comfortable walking shoes as Higashiyama involves cobblestone paths and gentle inclines. Morning visits to Maruyama Park before 8:00 AM offer the most peaceful hanami experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Arashiyama — Private car transfer to this iconic district on Kyoto's western outskirts. Walk through the ethereal Arashiyama Bamboo Grove at dawn when light filters through the towering stalks. Visit Tenryu-ji Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site with a stunning Zen garden and pond reflecting the surrounding cherry blossoms and mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Arashiyama Monkey Park Iwatayama — a family-friendly hike up the hillside where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Enjoy panoramic views over Kyoto and the Oi River below. Return down to the riverside for a private boat ride along the Hozu River, soaking in the forested gorge scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion by private car. Enjoy a relaxed evening exploring Pontocho Alley — a narrow lantern-lit dining corridor along the Kamo River — for pre-dinner drinks at a premium cocktail bar before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel Japanese breakfast with house-made tofu, seasonal pickles, steamed rice, and miso soup.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Shoraian — a beautifully situated riverside restaurant in Arashiyama serving refined tofu cuisine (yudofu) in a traditional wooden building overlooking the Oi River.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mizai or Kikunoi Honten — a three-Michelin-star Kyoto kaiseki restaurant offering an exquisite spring tasting menu with local river fish, bamboo shoots, and cherry blossom-infused dishes.

day_by_day.notes: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is best visited before 8:00 AM on weekends to avoid crowds. The Monkey Park involves a 20-minute uphill walk — suitable for most families but wear comfortable shoes. Private car hire for the day is strongly recommended over public transport on weekends during cherry blossom season.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Fushimi Inari Taisha — the iconic Shinto shrine famous for its thousands of vermillion torii gates winding up a forested mountain. Hire a private guide for an early morning walk through the upper trails, away from the tourist crowds, for a mystical and photogenic experience. The shrine is free to enter and open 24 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nishiki Market exploration — Kyoto's vibrant covered market known as 'Kyoto's Kitchen.' Browse over 100 stalls of premium local produce, artisan pickles, fresh tofu, wagashi sweets, and street food. Followed by a private visit to a renowned Kyoto pottery studio for a hands-on premium ceramics workshop with a master artisan.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from the rooftop terrace of a luxury Kyoto hotel bar (Hyatt Regency Kyoto or The Ritz-Carlton Kyoto), then a refined dinner in the Gion area.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before departing for Fushimi Inari — fresh pastries, seasonal fruit, green tea.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ganko Fushimi Yashiki — a beautifully restored historic restaurant near Fushimi Inari serving premium sushi and traditional Japanese cuisine in a samurai-era building.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Ritz-Carlton Kyoto's Mizuki restaurant — an elegant setting serving contemporary Japanese cuisine with curated sake and Japanese whisky pairings.

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is best visited before 7:00 AM on Sundays. The full hike to the summit takes 2–3 hours; a partial hike to Yotsutsuji intersection (about 45 minutes) offers excellent views and is family-friendly. Book the pottery workshop in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Nijo Castle visit — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and former residence of the Tokugawa shoguns. Explore the ornate Ninomaru Palace with its famous 'nightingale floors' designed to chirp underfoot as an anti-intruder alarm. The surrounding gardens are typically in late cherry blossom bloom in mid-April, creating spectacular scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Zen meditation session and garden tour at Ryoanji Temple, home to Japan's most celebrated rock garden. Followed by a visit to the Golden Pavilion (Kinkakuji) — the iconic gold-leaf-covered Zen temple reflected in its mirror pond, surrounded by manicured gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private geisha (geiko) dinner experience — arranged through your hotel concierge, this rare cultural event allows a small group to dine with a geiko and maiko who perform traditional dances, play instruments, and engage in refined conversation through an interpreter.

meals.breakfast: Full Japanese breakfast at the hotel — grilled salmon, pickled vegetables, rice, miso soup, and seasonal fruit.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Sarasa Nishijin — a beautifully restored former sento (public bathhouse) converted into a stylish café serving premium Japanese-Western fusion cuisine in a stunning ceramic-tiled interior.
meals.dinner: Private geisha dinner at a Gion ochaya (tea house) — a curated multi-course meal with sake and traditional entertainment. Arranged exclusively through the hotel concierge (must be booked weeks in advance).

day_by_day.notes: The private geisha dinner is one of Japan's most exclusive cultural experiences and requires advance booking through a trusted intermediary or your hotel concierge. Dress smartly. Nijo Castle is closed on Tuesdays — Monday visit is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Bullet train (Shinkansen) departure from Kyoto Station to Hiroshima — approximately 1 hour 15 minutes on the Nozomi Shinkansen. Reserve a private Green Car (first class) compartment for comfort. Arrive in Hiroshima mid-morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park — a profoundly moving and historically essential experience. Begin with a guided tour of the Peace Memorial Museum, which chronicles the events of August 6, 1945 with powerful artifacts and personal testimonies. Walk through the Peace Memorial Park, visiting the Atomic Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome), the Children's Peace Monument, and the Flame of Peace. This experience is deeply impactful for families and older children.
day_by_day.evening: Ferry crossing to Miyajima Island — visit the iconic Itsukushima Shrine and its famous 'floating' torii gate rising from the sea. Explore the island as the day-trippers depart and the atmosphere becomes serene. Overnight stay on Miyajima at a premium ryokan.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast in Kyoto before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Hiroshima at Nagarekawa Kappo Hasegawa — a refined Hiroshima-style kaiseki restaurant near the Peace Park serving seasonal local cuisine including premium oysters and Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki.
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner at your Miyajima ryokan (Miyajima Coral Hotel or Iwaso Ryokan) — a private multi-course dinner served in your room featuring Hiroshima oysters, seasonal sashimi, and local Saeki sake.

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum is recommended for children aged 10 and above due to the sensitive and sobering nature of the exhibits. Allocate at least 2–3 hours for the museum and park. The Miyajima torii gate is best photographed at high tide when it appears to float — check tide tables in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning on Miyajima Island before the day crowds arrive — hike or take the ropeway to the summit of Mount Misen for panoramic views over the Seto Inland Sea. Explore the island's ancient cedar forests and smaller shrines. Return to the shoreline to photograph the torii gate at low tide, when you can walk out to its base.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return ferry to Hiroshima, then Shinkansen to Tokyo (approximately 4 hours on the Nozomi, Green Car). Check in to your luxury Tokyo hotel (The Peninsula Tokyo, Aman Tokyo, or The Ritz-Carlton Tokyo). Freshen up and explore the immediate surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Evening at leisure in Tokyo — stroll through the Imperial Palace East Gardens (if still open) or explore the upscale Marunouchi district. Enjoy cocktails at the Aman Tokyo sky bar with panoramic city views before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese ryokan breakfast at your Miyajima accommodation — steamed rice, miso soup, grilled fish, pickles, and seasonal vegetables.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Miyajima's Kakiya — a renowned oyster restaurant serving Hiroshima's famous fresh oysters grilled, fried, and raw, with local sake.
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner in Tokyo at Joël Robuchon Tokyo (Ebisu Garden Place) — a legendary three-Michelin-star French-Japanese fusion restaurant offering the ultimate luxury dining experience in Tokyo.

day_by_day.notes: Book Shinkansen Green Car seats in advance, especially for the Hiroshima–Tokyo route. Tokyo hotel check-in is typically from 15:00 — arrange luggage forwarding (takuhaibin) from Kyoto hotel to Tokyo hotel if needed to travel light on the Shinkansen.

day_by_day.morning: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street — Visit Tokyo's oldest and most significant Buddhist temple in the historic Asakusa district. Arrive early morning for a peaceful atmosphere and stunning golden hour photography. Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate) and the 250-meter Nakamise shopping street lined with premium traditional craft shops, wagashi sweet makers, and artisan souvenir vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — Embark on a private guided culinary adventure through the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample premium tuna sashimi, uni (sea urchin), tamagoyaki, fresh oysters, wagyu beef skewers, and artisan Japanese condiments. Your guide will explain the history and culture of Japan's legendary fish market. Followed by a visit to nearby Hamarikyu Gardens — a stunning traditional garden with a teahouse on a tidal pond.
day_by_day.evening: Tokyo Tower or Tokyo Skytree observation deck at sunset for panoramic city views. Followed by an exclusive dinner in the upscale Ginza district.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at your Tokyo luxury hotel — extensive Japanese and Western buffet with premium ingredients, freshly baked pastries, and made-to-order egg station.
meals.lunch: Premium sushi lunch at Sushi Saito or Sushi Yoshitake (Ginza) — two of Tokyo's most celebrated and exclusive sushi counters offering the finest omakase sushi experience in Japan. Reserve months in advance.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten (Ginza) or Sushi Sho — legendary Tokyo sushi institutions offering intimate omakase counter experiences with the world's finest aged and seasonal sushi.

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is best visited before 8:00 AM to avoid crowds. The Tsukiji Outer Market is busiest in the morning — aim to arrive between 9:00–11:00 AM. Top-tier Tokyo sushi restaurants require reservations made months in advance and often require a Japanese-speaking contact or hotel concierge to book.

day_by_day.morning: Imperial Palace East Gardens and surroundings — Explore the beautifully maintained gardens of the Imperial Palace in the heart of Tokyo, with cherry blossom trees still potentially in late bloom. Stroll through the historic Kitanomaru Park and across the iconic Nijubashi Bridge. Visit the nearby Yasukuni Shrine and its excellent Yushukan military history museum for deeper historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Harajuku and Omotesando — Visit the Meiji Shrine, a serene forested Shinto sanctuary dedicated to Emperor Meiji, for a peaceful cultural contrast to the city's energy. Walk down Omotesando Avenue — Tokyo's most elegant tree-lined boulevard — for premium shopping at flagship stores including Louis Vuitton, Prada, and Japanese luxury brands. Visit the Omotesando Hills complex for architecture and high-end retail.
day_by_day.evening: Shibuya Crossing experience at peak evening hours — witness the world's busiest pedestrian scramble from the Mag's Park rooftop or Shibuya Sky observation deck. Followed by a farewell dinner in a private dining room.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel Japanese breakfast — house-made tofu, grilled fish, seasonal miso soup, and premium green tea.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Tableaux (Daikanyama) or Florilège — a two-Michelin-star contemporary French-Japanese restaurant in Minami-Aoyama offering a stunning open-kitchen tasting menu with Japanese-sourced ingredients.
meals.dinner: Premium wagyu dinner at Aragawa (Shimbashi) — one of Tokyo's most legendary and exclusive steakhouses serving Kobe beef from their own ranch, considered among the finest beef restaurants in the world. Or Ginza Kojyu for a refined kaiseki farewell dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Shrine is free to enter and open daily from sunrise to sunset. The Shibuya Sky observation deck requires advance ticket booking, especially on weekends. Aragawa is one of the world's most expensive restaurants — reservations are essential and dress code is strictly formal.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — Leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Last-minute premium shopping in Ginza: visit Itoya (the legendary 12-floor stationery and art supply flagship), Mitsukoshi Department Store's basement food hall (depachika) for exquisite Japanese food souvenirs, wagashi, premium teas, and sake to bring home. Visit Tsutaya Books in Daikanyama for curated Japanese art and design books.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Narita or Haneda Airport with ample time before departure. Enjoy the airport's premium lounges and duty-free shopping for last-minute Japanese spirits, cosmetics, and confectionery.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tokyo. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day journey through Japan's most iconic cultural, historical, and natural experiences.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final breakfast at the hotel — full Japanese and Western spread with premium seasonal fruit, artisan cheeses, and freshly brewed specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at a premium Ginza restaurant — Sushi Kanesaka or Ten-Ichi Ginza Honten (the original tempura restaurant established in 1930), serving perfectly fried seasonal vegetables and premium seafood tempura in an elegant counter setting.
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight premium dining (Business/First Class).

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport transfer and check-in. Haneda Airport is closer to central Tokyo (35–45 minutes) than Narita (60–90 minutes) — factor this into your departure timing. Luggage forwarding services (takuhaibin) can send purchases directly to the airport, saving you from carrying heavy bags on your final day.
